newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks fall as Wall Street slides.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks fall as Wall Street slides.

text.p: European share markets fell sharply on Friday as investors cashed in on this week's record run, taking their cue from a big drop on Wall Street.
London managed a quick spurt to within a whisker of the 5,000-point barrier in early trade but it soon fell back, a trend which accelerated when the Dow took its tumble.
On the foreign exchanges the dollar had a dull day enlivened only by comments from German Chancellor Helmut Kohl indicating he was unworried by the mark's sharp fall in recent months.
Wall Street encouraged the profit-takers on European bourses as the Dow Jones Industrial average fell below 8,000 points, breached earlier this week.
Towards the European close the Dow was down 85.94 points or 1.07 percent at 7,934.83 on profit-taking prompted by disappointment over earnings from high-tech companies.
Paris was the chief casualty among the leading stock markets as investors fretted over possible company tax hikes aimed at fixing the French budget for European monetary union.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn is expected to announce on Monday (0800 GMT) a package aimed at cutting the public deficit, which is threatening to hit 3.6 percent of gross domestic product -- far above the 3.0 percent target for joining the single European currency.

The newspaper Le Monde said the government would finalise on Saturday a package of measures to reduce the 1997 deficit by about 30 billion francs ($5 billion). Most of this year's measures are expected to be on the revenue side, with an extra "euro surcharge" on corporate tax expected to raise about 12 billion francs, officials said.
The thought of higher company taxes chilled the Paris bourse, and by late afternoon the CAC-40 index was down 81.90 points (2.77 percent) at 2,876.69.

London managed a strong morning performance and the FTSE-100 index hit a record intraday high of 4,998.1. But for the third time this week the FTSE failed to break the 5,000 barrier and the buying, dictated largely by technical factors, faded away.
Led by Wall Street, the FTSE was down 84.1 points or 1.7 percent at 4,864.9 by late afternoon.
Some analysts said a breach of 5,000, seemingly an inevitability earlier in the week, was now looking more distant.

"I would be surprised if the market really takes off from here," said Gary Dugan, London-based investment strategist at JP Morgan. "The market is cheap but I think it has to get cheaper still before there is a strong case to buy."

German shares, which closed at a record high on Thursday, also suffered from profit-taking. The DAX index of blue chips closed down 30.78 points or 0.73 percent at 4,196.53. The IBIS index, which measures post-bourse electronic trade, was down 1.71 percent at 4,131.94 by late afternoon.
"I think the market looks a bit tired ... The market needs to take a rest before moving higher" said one Frankfurt dealer.

On the foreign exchanges the dollar gained against the mark after Chancellor Kohl said a somewhat stronger dollar was not an earth-shaking matter. This seemed to confirm market suspicions that Germany is not too worried about the mark's recent steep fall against the dollar and other European currencies, which in any case has helped the country's exporters.

"When exports used to go badly because of a weak dollar, people complained," Kohl told a news conference. "Now things are going a bit the other way, which is not earth-shaking. It does not mean that we should start moaning again."
The dollar was at 1.7970 marks, down from 1.7998 at the European close on Thursday but up from earlier on Friday.

It was also at 115.77 yen, down from 116.07 on Thursday. This followed the annual report from the Japanese Economic Planning Agency (EPA), which said the country's economic recovery was close to self-sustaining.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 115.77 yen and 1.7970 marks compared with 116.07 yen and 1.7998 marks in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 84.1 points or 1.7 percent at 4,864.9 after hitting a record intradday high of 4,998.1.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index of floor trade closed down 30.78 points or 0.73 percent at 4,196.53. The IBIS index, which measures post-bourse electronic trade, was down 1.71 percent at 4,131.94.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 81.90 points (2.77 percent) at 2,876.69.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $324.20 an ounce compared with a morning fix at $323.45. Silver was nine cents higher at $4.28.
($ = 6.056 French Francs)
